newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara to meet bankers on Friday-sources.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara to meet bankers on Friday-sources.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia will be meeting the heads of selected banks on Friday to discuss routine foreign exchange activities of the banks, banking sources said on Thursday.
"Bank Negara is calling a number of banks to talk about their activities and exposure in the forex market. This is quite routine," said a banking source.
The source said the meeting could last over two days.
Banking sources said the recent volatility of the forex market was one reason prompting the central bank to call for the meeting.
Speculation of the meeting sparked off rumours that Bank Negara would introduce capital controls including restriction on swap transactions to offshore players.
The talk triggered heavy dollar sales and pushed up swap rates as offshore players covered their positions, dealers said.
But the banking sources said Bank Negara was unlikely to impose capital controls like those in Thailand.
Research house I.D.E.A. said any move to limit offshore borrowings of the ringgit would create a two-tier market, one for domestic players and another for foreign ones.

"Certainly this will ensure that ringgit falls into the right hands. But this will drastically reduce liquidity for offshore in terms of hedging facilities, thereby digging graves for the (introduction of) upcoming financial instruments," it said in a report.
